name: Classify support tickets and build a human review queue with Apixly

parameters.content:
## Support ticket triage with Apixly

### How it works
This manual workflow turns a small batch of support tickets into one human review queue. It starts with three synthetic examples, validates the input, and sends one bounded classification request per ticket to Apixly's OpenAI-compatible API. The model suggests a category, priority, summary, and reply draft. Each result is checked against the original ticket ID and a strict output schema. API failures, incomplete answers, and invalid JSON remain in the queue for manual triage. The final report includes every ticket and counts successful classifications and fallbacks.

### Setup
1. Create an n8n Header Auth credential. Set Name to Authorization and Value to the word Bearer, one space, and your own Apixly API key. Select it in Classify with Apixly. Never paste keys into workflow fields.
2. In Configure demo tickets, confirm the current model ID and API endpoint. Start with the synthetic examples. Each run makes one potentially billable request per ticket.
3. Click Execute workflow and open Build human review queue. Review all drafts before using them. No customer messages, refunds, or account changes are sent automatically.

Replace sample tickets only with data you are authorized to process. Model suggestions can be wrong; reported usage is not verified billing. Created by the Apixly team.

### 1. Configure and validate
Set the endpoint, model, and synthetic tickets here. Input validation stops empty, oversized, or duplicate-ID batches before API requests.

### 2. Request suggestions
The prompt treats ticket text as untrusted data. Select your Header Auth credential in the HTTP node. Failed requests proceed to manual triage; automatic retries are off.

### 3. Validate and review
Strict schema checks preserve ticket identity. Every ticket appears in one review queue, including API failures. Review drafts yourself; this workflow never sends them.
